candidate_evidence.quote: [DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT] zinc and ascorbate: oral zinc and ascorbate
Zinc has been consumed by the public as an essential mineral (and thus is category A drug) in concentrations which allows this effect with Temozolomide.

candidate_flag.reason: Oral zinc and ascorbate are registered as a dietary supplement; if either is judged a licensed medicine given with an antitumour hypothesis (zinc to potentiate temozolomide), it would be a candidate and the trial would pass S6.

role_evidence.quote: [DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT] zinc and ascorbate: oral zinc and ascorbate
We hope to demonstrate the anti-tumor activity of zinc that will enhance the activity of temozolomide chemotherapy in adult glioblastoma patients.

agents.drug_class_hint: trace element / mineral dietary supplement (oral zinc)
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: Zinc (Zn) has a crucial role in the biology of p53, in that p53 binds to DNA through a structurally complex domain stabilized by zinc atom.

flag.reason: Registered as dietary supplement but given with an antitumour hypothesis; if judged a licensed medicine it would be experimental_combination (candidate).

role_evidence.quote: [DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT] zinc and ascorbate: oral zinc and ascorbate
Vitamin C could add to this by priming the immune system for lymphocyte- linked cancer killing.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: The vitamin c increases the number of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes and enhances the activation of the immune system.

flag.reason: Oral vitamin C registered as dietary supplement with a stated antitumour (immune) hypothesis; if judged a licensed medicine it would be a candidate.

role_evidence.quote: We propose a single arm phase II clinical trial in 30 newly diagnosed GBM patients who will be treated with the standard chemo-radiotherapy with the addition of zinc and vitamin C.

agents.drug_class_hint: alkylating agent, GBM standard of care

coder_notes: Registry phase NA (brief summary calls it a single-arm phase II). Temozolomide is not a registered intervention but every patient receives standard chemoradiotherapy, so it is listed as soc_backbone. Zinc and ascorbate are one registered intervention split into two rows; not clear whether a single combined product (fixed_dose_combination set false). If zinc/vitamin C were accepted as candidates, regimen would be combination with partners temozolomide and radiotherapy, and target_engagement could be 'yes' (blood T-cell count, IL-6, TNF as immune pharmacodynamic markers for vitamin C); coded 'unclear' because outcomes are not explicitly linked to the agents. p53 is mentioned only as rationale in the brief summary, not as a biomarker endpoint or requirement.
